findings.what: Promotion recovery still lets forged original=true metadata and an attacker-controlled backup delete and replace a live registry-bound artifact, while its original=false rule rejects a genuine interrupted promotion of a newly created artifact.
findings.why: For an original=true/applied entry, _validate_recovery_artifacts accepts backup.exists() as sufficient provenance at lines 281-284. Public restart then enters _rollback, calls discard_workspace(live), and backup.replace(live) at lines 119-124. A portable case can therefore forge the exact ordered P1 or P7 write set, place arbitrary regular bytes under attempt-1/promotion-backup/data/sources.json or README.md, and have run_workflow replace the legitimate live artifact before state identity validation. Conversely, the original=false branch requires live absence, so a genuine crash after _apply has installed a brand-new P7 output and journaled it applied is rejected forever. The new tests cover false original=false deletion claims and existing-original rollback only; they never cover forged original=true backup replacement or genuine newly-created-artifact recovery. This violates AC3 atomic recovery and AC5 journalist-content preservation. Redesign the recovery authority so no case-supplied original bit or backup alone authorizes destructive replacement, while retaining restart-idempotent recovery for producer-created states; add public-restart proofs for both forged original=true P1/P7 backups and a genuine interrupted new-artifact promotion.

findings.what: The consolidated dynamic-review boundary still exposes two live names for the same attestation field instead of a clean alias-free contract.
findings.why: _REVIEW_FIELDS accepts both attestation and independent_attestation, and _review_owner_result translates the former into the latter at lines 146-149. The split is reachable: agents/anomaly-data-reviewer.md documents attestation, while the canonical demo fake in tests/test_pipeline_walk.py returns independent_attestation. This is a compatibility alias and a second schema authority, contrary to AC8 and the explicit no-alias clean cutover. Select one canonical field, migrate the reviewer instructions and every caller/test to it, and delete the translation and duplicate-field branch.

findings.what: The P7 completion matrix still does not prove that changing a chart descendant invalidates completion.
findings.why: P7_OUTPUT_MUTATIONS removes the whole charts directory but never changes, adds, removes, or changes the kind of a descendant. An existence-only implementation would satisfy the current row, although identities._completion_identity correctly hashes descendant path, kind, and bytes. Add one deterministic completed-case row that mutates a chart file and asserts P7 invalidation plus README demotion; this is consumer-observable regression coverage, not a production defect.

findings.what: run_workflow still resolves the same snapshot twice on every loop iteration.
findings.why: The first resolve_workflow call is needed only to establish entry_phase, but after entry_phase is set its result is discarded and the same snapshot is resolved again at line 198. Restrict the preliminary resolution to the first iteration, preserving fresh gate filtering while deleting avoidable computation and supporting the lean-consolidation objective.

findings.what: A retained test name still says events participate in resume authority.
findings.why: test_resume_reads_progress_from_state_and_events_not_reports neither reads nor asserts events; the production and installed contracts correctly make state.completed authoritative and events observational. Rename it to state-not-report wording so the suite does not preserve stale authority terminology.
